mintAuthority.summary: YUSD mint authority terminates in a single 3-of-5 Safe (0x4Fe78eF65BD8EDDED480efaB030BA680646503c8) on every deployment. Ethereum and BSC each mint through a chain-local AegisMinting contract that requires a whitelisted order signed by trusted signer 0xb28c97E348C3078fC1F6Fcc61b79c8a0DA35008e; Avalanche is a LayerZero V2 OFT that mints on peer delivery. None of the four contracts is a proxy, but the Safe can repoint mint logic because YUSD.setMinter is onlyOwner, so mint-critical logic is Safe-changeable with no timelock.

controls.label: AegisMinting (BSC)
controls.capDescription: No on-chain supply ceiling; the BSC AegisMinting contract is the sole minter of the BSC YUSD token and its mint limits are administered by the same Aegis admin Safe that owns the Ethereum deployment.

routeChecks.attestorQuorum: BSC AegisConfig 0xB9f1E8417ABaedF6Fd838212267cA8260c4ca9da trustedSigner() = 0xb28c97E348C3078fC1F6Fcc61b79c8a0DA35008e, the same trusted signer as the Ethereum deployment; minting requires that single signer's signature over the order.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: AegisMinting(BSC).owner() and defaultAdmin() both return the Aegis admin Safe 0x4Fe78eF65BD8EDDED480efaB030BA680646503c8; BSC AegisConfig.owner() returns the same Safe.

controls.evidence: At BSC block 111124154: YUSD(0xab3dbcd9...).minter() = 0x02bf8f0e046F471709E578b1E633077096ce65CF and YUSD.owner() = 0x4Fe78eF65BD8EDDED480efaB030BA680646503c8. AegisMinting(BSC).yusd() = 0xAB3dBcD9B096C3fF76275038bf58eAC10D22C61f, .owner() = .defaultAdmin() = 0x4Fe78eF65BD8EDDED480efaB030BA680646503c8, .aegisConfig() = 0xB9f1E8417ABaedF6Fd838212267cA8260c4ca9da. controls.label: YUSD Avalanche LayerZero OFT
controls.capDescription: The Avalanche deployment is a LayerZero V2 OFT that mints on delivery of a message from a configured peer; there is no on-chain supply ceiling and the peer/DVN configuration is set by the LayerZero delegate.

review.evidence: Prior review left the BSC and Avalanche authority chains unenumerated. Resolved 2026-07-20 by direct reads. Ethereum (block 25575161): YUSD.owner() = 0x4Fe78eF65BD8EDDED480efaB030BA680646503c8, YUSD.minter() = AegisMinting 0xC4Df68e592245cA5202fE8b7C438d2b799820fc2, totalSupply 34,129,715.738490831724848552. BSC (block 111124154): YUSD.owner() = 0x4Fe78eF65BD8EDDED480efaB030BA680646503c8, YUSD.minter() = AegisMinting 0x02bf8f0e046F471709E578b1E633077096ce65CF whose owner() and defaultAdmin() are the same Safe and whose AegisConfig 0xB9f1E8417ABaedF6Fd838212267cA8260c4ca9da has owner() = the Safe and trustedSigner() = 0xb28c97E348C3078fC1F6Fcc61b79c8a0DA35008e, identical to Ethereum. Avalanche (block 90804258): the token is a native LayerZero V2 OFT with owner() = the Safe and EndpointV2.delegates() = the Safe. All four contracts read zero at the EIP-1967 implementation slot, so none is a standard proxy; the verified Ethereum YUSD source shows setMinter(address) is onlyOwner and mint(address,uint256) is onlyMinter, so the Safe can substitute mint logic without an upgrade and without a delay. Every mint surface therefore reduces to one 3-of-5 Safe plus one trusted signer. Reconciliation cadence and prudential supervision remain unevidenced and are deliberately left "unknown" rather than inferred from the Accountable real-time dashboard; that is recorded in the profile fields, not as a blocking question.
